texts: bad: two losses in the reported lore — the general claim "mire-essence with salt-bloom burns slowly" is recorded as one single burn event instead of a rule covering every such essence, and the "with salt-bloom" restriction is torn off into a separate claim that mire-essence carries salt-bloom, which widens your claim to mire-essence at large. A finite relative clause keeps the restriction on the claim and forces the rule form: "On day 590 of Year 2, Coraline Ash told Eli that mire-essence that contains salt-bloom burns slowly." Separate note: "day 590 of Year 2" lands in the day-of-month slot, which cannot hold a day-of-year count.

good. the telling is dated and attributed, and the shielding — spire group, the Northcove, and the "against the north wind" target — stays inside what Coraline said rather than being asserted as fact, with only the typing of the named and definite things projecting out.

mixed: the report itself is right, but "of the Northcove" escapes the report — the parse asserts as a world fact that the lanterns belong to the Northcove, although only Coraline said so. If you want that link in the knowledge base, state it in its own sentence and leave the report to the burning: "The Northcove has lanterns. Coraline Ash told Eli that the lanterns burn plain mire-essence."

mixed: this reads as one particular lantern that happens to burn at full rate, not as the world rule you mean — "a lantern" plus a verb is always a single witness, and the condition packed into the participle "burning at full rate" gets no proper condition slot. Make the condition a finite clause with a plain connective: "Coraline Ash told Eli that when a lantern burns at full rate, it produces strong mist-light." The rate phrase "at full rate" has no licensed slot either way, so it stays a known gap whichever wording you use.

good. the writing, the answer group, Eli's notebook and the in-the-notebook location are all covered on a past event; "the answers" does mint a fresh set with no link back to what Coraline told her, but the sentence states no such link.
